Load 1.8 s, one sentence 0.08 s on CPU. XPOS is the NKJP-style tag TermoPL expects. Three things that did not go as instructed

Download budget exceeded. Total downloads were about 5 GB against the ~4 GB limit. The overshoot comes from COMBO: 205 MB of wheels plus 3.36 GB of models (I had expected about 1.1 GB; the segmenter model and the base encoder are a further 1.1 GB each). The 3.36 GB model cache has been deleted again; the 1.0 GB venv is kept. rm -rf resources/tools/combo removes the rest.
Two archive copies were written outside resources/tools/ by the mandated download commands (library defaults, noticed afterwards, left untouched because they sit in your personal caches):

~/.cache/huggingface/hub/blobs/16/162b914981fee565eeda4a379678d7e24fd1a01e3ed48cf956349363eb9105c4 (416,036,108 bytes, Stanza default.zip), plus the small ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--stanfordnlp--stanza-pl/ entry that points to it. Stanza 1.15.0 downloads through huggingface_hub, which caches there regardless of model_dir.
~/Library/Caches/pip/http-v2/6/b/f/7/a/6bf7a2b408c3b3cb9e4a423e0c004cb23aa2b9b143d351354224e7c1.body (573,718,074 bytes, the pl_core_news_lg wheel in pip’s HTTP cache). Both are safe to delete; together they hold about 1 GB.

pyarrow==26.0.1 appeared in the main venv at 12:32:37. It was not installed by this work (the only pip action here was python -m spacy download pl_core_news_lg at 12:26). spacy, stanza, torch, numpy and pandas are unchanged (pip freeze diff before/after shows only pl_core_news_lg and pyarrow).



Disk use under resources/tools/ (after clean-up)







Path

All downloaded archives inside resources/tools/ were deleted after unpacking (TermoPL_Mac_OS_X.zip, Stanza pl/default.zip, Concraft-MacOSX.zip, format-examples.zip).




2. TermoPL 8.1.1

Page: https://zil.ipipan.waw.pl/TermoPL (“Downloads (current version: 8.1.1)”, page last edited 2025-10-30). The jar’s About class contains the string Version 8.1.1.
Downloaded: https://zil.ipipan.waw.pl/TermoPL?action=AttachFile&do=get&target=TermoPL_Mac_OS_X.zip (9,429,888 bytes, “Mac OS X (arm_64)” package), unpacked to termopl/TermoPL_Mac_OS_X/. SHA-256 of TermoPL.jar: b46c5aab9a9dfa70ffc1ba51e180c4473201100edb8ccddd59ae562f768c6fb2.
Package contents: TermoPL.jar, libjmorfeusz.dylib and libmorfeusz2.dylib (both arm64), parse.py, TermoPL-user-manual.pdf (manual “TermoPL 8.1”, dated 22.09.2025), termopl_sw.txt / termopl_cp.txt / termopl_ct.txt (default stop words, compound prepositions, common terms), languages/.
Licence: BSD 2-clause, “Copyright (c) 2016, Institute of Computer Science, Polish Academy of Sciences”. Text: termopl/LICENSE.txt, from https://zil.ipipan.waw.pl/TermoPL?action=AttachFile&do=get&target=LICENSE.txt. The bundled Morfeusz 2 library is also BSD 2-clause (https://morfeusz.sgjp.pl/doc/license/).
Sources (src.zip from the same page) were read to confirm the behaviour described below; they are not kept on disk.


2.1 Input formats (manual section 2.1 and CorpusReader.java)
TermoPL needs morphologically tagged, disambiguated, lemmatised UTF-8 input. The format is chosen per file:








Format
Recognised by
What is read




CoNLL-U
extension .conllu
col 2 FORM, col 3 LEMMA, col 4 UPOS, col 5 XPOS (used as the NKJP-style tag), col 6 FEATS, col 7 HEAD, col 8 DEPREL, col 10 MISC (SpaceAfter=No, or start_char=..\|end_char=.., optional ner=). Multi-word-token lines 1-2 are handled. A comment line containing newdoc starts a new document. All 10 columns must be present.


Flat text
any other name whose lines have two tabs
form<TAB>lemma<TAB>tag, or form<TAB>#lemma<TAB>#tag#. Empty line (or &<TAB>&<TAB>interp) ends a sentence. A line starting with %% starts a new document.


Legacy flat
extension .tgt
form<TAB>lemma<TAB>tag[<TAB>nps], sentences end with a line eos.


XCES / CCL
extension .ccl or <?xml … <cesAna
<tok><orth>, <lex disamb="1"><base>, <ctag>


NKJP TEI
<?xml … <teiCorpus
ann_morphosyntax-style fs type="morph" with disamb


Plain text
anything else
handed to parse.py (Stanza) to produce a .conllu next to the file. Does not work in batch mode in 8.1.1, see 2.4.



The tag is the NKJP/SGJP positional tag with : separators, e.g. subst:sg:gen:m3, adj:pl:nom:f:pos. The built-in grammar only looks at the class (subst, ger, adj, adja, ppas), at case = gen, at agreement in number/case/gender, and at the form -. The default tagset is defined “by values”, so the order of categories inside the tag does not matter.
What can produce this input here:







Source
Result




Stanza pl (PDB)
Directly usable. Stanza’s XPOS column is already the NKJP-style tag, so CoNLL.write_doc2conll output is read as is. Stanza’s lemmatiser makes errors on domain words (below).


Morfeusz2 alone
Not usable: it lists all readings, it does not disambiguate. Usable as a lemma check on top of a tagger (txt2conllu.py --morfeusz-lemmas) or as input to Concraft (section 5).


Morfeusz2 + Concraft-pl
Usable via the flat format (concraft/concraft_tag.py).


spaCy pl_core_news_lg
Usable after conversion: token.tag_ holds only the class (SUBST, ADJ …), so the tag has to be rebuilt from token.morph (termopl/spacy2flat.py).



Scripts written for this (all in termopl/, run with the main venv python):

txt2conllu.py IN_DIR OUT_DIR [--no-depparse] [--morfeusz-lemmas]: Stanza, models from resources/tools/stanza_resources, no network access. --morfeusz-lemmas replaces a Stanza lemma by the Morfeusz2 lemma when exactly one Morfeusz lemma is compatible with the tag Stanza chose (gerunds are left alone).
conllu2flat.py IN_DIR OUT_DIR: CoNLL-U to flat form<TAB>lemma<TAB>tag.
spacy2flat.py IN_DIR OUT_DIR: spaCy to flat format.
run_termopl.sh TXT_DIR WORK_DIR OUT_TSV [MAX_LEN=4] [CONTRAST]: the whole chain, see 2.5.

Why the Morfeusz lemma check matters. On the 402-token test corpus Stanza produced these lemmas (log of txt2conllu.py --morfeusz-lemmas):
lemma chloroplastach: chloroplasta -> chloroplast
lemma fotosyntezy: fotosyntez -> fotosynteza
lemma dwutlenek: dwutlenka -> dwutlenek
lemma glukoza: glukoze -> glukoza
lemma błonę: błońa -> błona
lemma błonie: błoń -> błona
lemma cytoplazmy: cytoplazm -> cytoplazma
lemma utleniana: utlenieć -> utleniać
18 of 402 lemmas were replaced. Without the check TermoPL splits one term into several rows (test/out/stanza_lemmas_gt.txt):
1   1   dwutlenka węgiel    [dwutlenek węgla]   4.0 2   4   0   0
8   3   dwutlenek węgiel    [dwutlenek węgla]   2.0 2   3   1   1
6   3   błona komórkowy [błona komórkowa]   2.0 2   3   1   1
12  3   błońa komórkowy [błonę komórkowa]   2.0 2   2   0   0
With the check (test/out/morf_lemmas_gt.txt) these are single rows: dwutlenek węgiel 6.0 (freq 7), błona komórkowy 5.0 (freq 6).


2.2 Batch mode and options (manual section 7, BatchParameters.java, tested)
java [JVM options] -jar TermoPL.jar [program options] file...
Any argument switches the program to batch mode (no GUI). Everything after the first non-option argument is treated as an input file or directory. Options can also be put in a file given with -conf FILE (one option per line, input paths as -in PATH); command-line options win.








Purpose
Option
Notes (tested unless marked)




Output: text table
-exp FILE
UTF-8, tab-separated, no header line


Output: binary term set
-out FILE.trm
can be reused as input or as contrastive set


Output: all forms / sentences / groups
-expf FILE, -exps FILE, -expg FILE.xml
-expg not tested


Columns of -exp
-save "# rank sf bf cvalue comp length freq_s freq_in context"
one quoted argument; columns are always written in this fixed order whatever order you list

-sf
no base (nominative) forms


Multi-word terms only
-mw
keeps length >= 2


Top-ranked only
-tr N
keeps terms with rank <= N, not N rows (-tr 10 gave 58 rows on the test corpus because of ties)


Sorting
-sort COL (ascending), -SORT COL (descending)
rank, term, cvalue, comp, length, freq_s, freq_in, context; not tested


Extraction method
-method gt (grammar templates, default) or -method ud (UD trees)
ud needs HEAD/DEPREL, i.e. Stanza depparse


Nested-phrase search (C-value variant)
-srch npmi1\|npmi2\|npmi3\|nonpmi1\|nonpmi2
default npmi3; nonpmi1 = all sub-phrases, nonpmi2 = trim left to right


NPMI preference factor
-pf N
default 120; not tested


Context counting for C-value
-cntx 1\|2\|3
default 1 (max of distinct left and right contexts)


Stop words
-SW (bundled termopl_sw.txt) or -sw FILE
without either, no stop-word filtering


Compound prepositions
-CP or -cp FILE



Common (general) terms
-CT or -ct FILE



Custom grammar / tagset
-grammar FILE, -tagset FILE
examples in languages/pl/; not tested


Contrastive corpus
-comp FILE + -cc ll\|tfitf\|csmw\|tw\|no
FILE is a .trm or a text export of another run (3, 8, 9 or 10 columns); adds the comp column. The manual prints csmv, the program only accepts csmw (Bad option: -cc csmv).


Contrastive thresholds
-frq (frequencies instead of C-values), -freq N, -cval X
not tested


Determiners (UD method)
-det include\|exclude\|article, -detr N
not tested


Case
-ignc yes\|no
default yes


WordNet grouping
-wdn plwordnet.xml, -group
not tested; needs the plWordNet XML


Workspace for relative paths
-wrk DIR
not tested


Language
-lang pl
default pl


Python for plain text
-python PATH
accepted but ignored in 8.1.1 (2.4)



There is no option for maximum term length. Bad option: -maxlen is what an invented option returns. A min/max length filter exists only in the GUI’s Terms window (Preferences.minLength = 2, maxLength = -1, applied only together with “multi-word terms only”). The cap therefore has to be applied to the exported table using the length column. Longer phrases are still found and still count as contexts for their nested sub-phrases, which is how C-value is meant to work.
C-value as implemented (manual 3.1): C(p) = l(p) * (f(p) - (1/|LP|) * sum f(lp)) if p is nested in other phrases, else l(p) * f(p); l(p) = log2(length) for multi-word terms and 0.1 for one-word terms.

2.4 Pitfalls found while testing

Start it from TermoPL_Mac_OS_X/. libjmorfeusz.dylib loads libmorfeusz2.dylib by bare name, which macOS resolves against the current directory. From any other directory (with or without -Djava.library.path=<app dir>) you get java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError: no jmorfeusz in java.library.path, exit status 0, and an output file with wrong content (rank 0, unsorted, different C-values). -sf (simplified forms only) fails the same way from another directory. Always check stderr.
Plain-text input does not work in batch mode. -python PATH is parsed but never passed on (BatchParameters.python is not referenced by any other class in the 8.1.1 jar; checked with javap). Result: Python interpreted not selected., exit status 0, empty output. Workaround: tag first, pass .conllu. This is also preferable because the bundled parse.py calls stanza.download() on every run.
A directory argument is read recursively and every file in it is used, including .DS_Store or leftover .txt files. An unrecognised file triggers pitfall 2 and the whole run yields an empty output. Keep the input directory clean (only .conllu).
Wildcards are not expanded by the program (File does not exist -- …/*.conllu followed by a NullPointerException). Give a directory, or let the shell expand the pattern (do not quote it).
Row order among ties is not stable between a directory argument and a shell-expanded file list (same rows, same values, different order inside a rank). Repeated runs with the same argument are byte-identical. Sort downstream by C-value and term if a stable order is needed.
~/.TermoPL-8: if the GUI is ever started it saves its preferences there, and batch mode loads that file first. It does not exist on this machine. Settings that batch mode does not override (for example the min/max length used with -mw) would then come from the GUI.
Stanza lemmatises gerunds as nouns (oddychanie), Morfeusz/Concraft/spaCy as infinitives (oddychać). TermoPL prints the right base form in both cases, but mixing the conventions in one corpus splits terms. txt2conllu.py --morfeusz-lemmas therefore never touches gerunds.



2.5 Batch run on a directory of text files with a 4-word cap
cd resources/tools/termopl
./run_termopl.sh /path/to/txt_dir /path/to/work_dir /path/to/terms_max4.tsv 4
# optional 5th argument: contrastive term set (.trm or text export), adds comp_ll
Verified on the test corpus: 3.8 s wall in total, output all terms: 127  kept (length <= 4): 127. The script tags with Stanza (--no-depparse --morfeusz-lemmas), runs the command from 2.3 from inside TermoPL_Mac_OS_X/, fails loudly if stderr contains an exception or the output is empty, then keeps rows with length <= 4, strips the brackets from the base form and adds a header (nr rank simplified_form base_form cvalue length freq_s freq_in contexts). It also writes work_dir/terms.trm (reusable as a contrastive set for another run) and work_dir/terms_all.tsv (unfiltered).
The filter itself, if you run TermoPL by hand with the -save list above (length is column 6, or column 7 when -comp is used):
awk -F'\t' '$6 <= 4' terms_all.tsv > terms_max4.tsv
Memory: the manual states about 1 GB of RAM per 500,000 tokens and suggests -Xmx5G -Xms4G for much larger corpora. Not measured here.

Licence flag: the Polish COMBO models are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial, share-alike). Whether that is acceptable for this project is a decision for the project owner.


6.2 KRNNT
https://github.com/kwrobel-nlp/krnnt (last push 2023-05-22, LGPL-3.0, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kwrobel-nlp/krnnt/master/LICENSE). Not on PyPI (https://pypi.org/pypi/krnnt/json returns 404). Not installed. Reasons:

setup.py (version 1.0.0) pins Keras==2.2.5 and, as extras, tensorflow==1.14.0 / tensorflow-gpu==1.12.0; requirements.txt pins numpy==1.16.4, h5py==2.9.0.
TensorFlow 1.14.0 on PyPI has wheels only for cp27 and cp33–cp37, on macosx_10_11_x86_64, manylinux1_x86_64, win_amd64. Nothing for Python 3.12 or arm64. h5py 2.9.0 stops at cp38, x86_64.
It also needs the external tools Maca and Toki (maca-analyse -qc morfeusz2-nkjp), which the README tells you to install by following a Dockerfile.
The README’s supported route is Docker (docker run -p 9003:9003 -it djstrong/krnnt:1.0.0); no Docker daemon here.

Trained models are attached to the GitHub releases (reana.zip 20 MB, preana.zip 21 MB, reana10.zip 146 MB); no separate model licence is stated in the README.




7. Licence flags (for a decision by the project owner)

UD_Polish-PDB is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Its LICENSE.txt and README (https://github.com/UniversalDependencies/UD_Polish-PDB) say so, and the README changelog records “License changed from GNU GPL 3.0 to CC BY-NC-SA 4.0” at release v2.4 (2019-05-15). All three neural pipelines’ Polish models are trained on it:

spaCy pl_core_news_lg 3.8.0 declares itself GNU GPL 3.0 and lists “UD Polish PDB v2.8” with licence “GNU GPL 3.0”. That does not match the treebank’s own statement for v2.4 and later.
Stanza’s stanza-pl model card declares Apache-2.0. The Stanza documentation page says the UD models are trained on Universal Dependencies v2.12, a release in which PDB is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
COMBO’s model card says CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, consistent with the treebank. Whether a model inherits the licence of its training data is a legal question that this check does not answer.

Concraft-pl model concraft-pl-model-SGJP-20220221.gz: no licence stated on the download page.
pl_nask: no licence in the package metadata.
GPL 3.0 (spaCy model, IPI PAN spaCy models, COMBO code) and LGPL 3.0 (KRNNT) are copyleft licences; relevant if tools or models are redistributed.
TermoPL, Morfeusz2 with SGJP, and the Concraft-pl code are BSD 2-clause. Outputs of TermoPL (term lists) are not covered by any statement on the TermoPL page.



8. Download accounting







Item
Bytes downloaded




TermoPL package, manual, licence, tagset, sources, languages, jars
10.7 MB


pl_core_news_lg wheel
573.7 MB


Stanza resources.json + pl/default.zip
416.5 MB


Metadata checks of IPI PAN spaCy archives (streamed, nothing stored)
116 MB measured for pl_spacy_model_morfeusz; pl_spacy_model and pl_nask (twice) not measured


Concraft binary, examples, model (plus 0.9 MB from an interrupted first attempt)
89 MB


COMBO wheels
205 MB


COMBO models from Hugging Face
3,364 MB


Total
about 4.8 GB measured, roughly 5 GB with the unmeasured streams

text:
Requirements


What you need besides the code in this repository. The published run (probka50) was made on macOS 26.5 (Apple Silicon, 18 GB RAM) with Python 3.12.2; nothing has been tested on Linux or Windows.

1. System software

2. Python environment

# or, for the exact environment of the published run:
pip install -r requirements-lock.txt
The location matters: run_termopl.sh and step 7 start helper scripts with <repository>/.venv/bin/python.
requirements.txt installs the spaCy model pl_core_news_lg 3.8.0 (GPL-3.0, about 570 MB) and Morfeusz2 with the SGJP dictionary. wordfreq brings its own Polish frequency data.


3. Files to download into resources/
These are not in the repository because of their size or licence. Paths are relative to the repository root. Full notes on each (how it was obtained, format, licence evidence, SHA-256) are in resources/*/README_*.md and resources/*/manifest.json.

“Optional” means the step logs the failure and continues without that method. “Required” means the step stops if the file is missing. On another operating system TermoPL needs the matching package from the same page and the APP path in run_termopl.sh changed accordingly.


4. Input data and credentials
Set these in the zrodlo section of config/biologia_sp.yaml; the committed file holds the paths of the machine that made the published run.







Setting
What it must point to




zrodlo.zpe_dir
A local dump of the ZPE platform with catalog.jsonl, subjects.json, materials/<id>.manifest.json, materials/<id>_<unit>.html and texts/<id>.txt. Read-only for the pipeline. The dump is not distributed with this repository.


zrodlo.env_file
A .env file with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... (the environment variable of the same name also works).


zrodlo.podstawa_pdf
Present in the configuration, but no step reads it at the moment.



API use is bounded by llm.limit_kosztu_usd in the configuration: a request batch is refused when the spend so far plus its estimated cost would pass the limit. The sample run cost about 2.4 USD. With --bez-llm no API call is made: step 5 is skipped and the other steps use only answers already in the local cache.


5. Running
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m jutro run --config config/biologia_sp.yaml --probka 50      # sample: 50 target + 300 contrast materials
python -m jutro run --config config/biologia_sp.yaml                  # full corpus
python -m jutro run --config config/biologia_sp.yaml --probka 50 --kroki raport   # one step only
Steps whose result already exists in data/<name>/<run>/ are skipped; --od-nowa forces them to run again. The sample run needed about 40 minutes of processing, most of it waiting for batch jobs in step 5, and about 40 MB in data/.
To rebuild only the site from the committed results in wyniki/ (no ZPE dump, models or API key needed):
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m jutro site --config config/biologia_sp.yaml --probka 50
This renders site/*.qmd with Quarto and replaces docs/, the folder GitHub Pages serves, with the result. Step 8 of a normal run does the same. The pages contain no hard-coded numbers; they read wyniki/<name>/<run>/ while rendering.


6. What is and is not repeatable

Sampling of materials, the benchmark sample, the gold-set worksheet and template choice use the seed ziarno from the configuration.
Language-model answers are not deterministic. They are cached under data/<name>/<run>/llm/, which is not published, so a fresh run asks the models again and labels can differ.
The versions of all libraries used by a run are saved in wyniki/<name>/<run>/przebieg.json.



7. Known problem that affects reproduction
Step 7 does not read the output of the UniPseudo generator. It takes the first rows of whichever CSV file is in resources/pseudo/unipseudo/. In the published run that was a six-letter smoke-test file, so the unipseudo rows in pseudoslowa.csv repeat three strings. On a clean checkout there is no such file and the method returns nothing. The other three generators are not affected.

title: Reproduce
text:
Configuration
Subject, school stage, grades, thresholds, models and the seed are parameters. To repeat the process for another subject, copy the file and change the cel section.


# Pilotaż JUTRO – konfiguracja przebiegu.
# Przedmiot i klasy są parametrami: żeby powtórzyć proces dla innego przedmiotu,
# skopiuj ten plik i zmień sekcję `cel` (oraz `klasa_szacowana`, jeśli ma być użyta).
#
# Uruchomienie:  python -m jutro run --config config/biologia_sp.yaml [--probka 50]

nazwa: biologia_sp
ziarno: 20261113

zrodlo:
  # Zrzut ZPE (catalog.jsonl + materials/*.html + texts/*.txt). Tylko do odczytu.
  zpe_dir: ~/Desktop/ibe/dashboards/podstawy_programowe/data/zpe
  # Plik .env z kluczem API (zmienna anthropic_api_key lub ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). Klucz nie jest kopiowany.
  env_file: ~/Desktop/ibe/dashboards/podstawy_programowe/.env
  # Podstawa programowa przedmiotu (PDF) – dodatkowy srebrny standard; null = pomiń.
  podstawa_pdf: ~/Desktop/ibe/dashboards/podstawy_programowe/in/Biologia_IBE_PIB.pdf

cel:
  przedmiot: Biologia            # etykieta przedmiotu w katalogu ZPE
  etap_kod: E2                   # E2 = szkoła podstawowa IV–VIII
  klasy: [5, 6, 7, 8]            # klasy docelowe (atrybut; filtr tylko jeśli filtruj_klasy: true)
  filtruj_klasy: false           # katalog ZPE nie ma klasy materiału – patrz klasa_szacowana
  typy_wyklucz:                  # typy materiałów adresowane do nauczyciela, nie do ucznia
    - "scenariusz Lekcja:Enter"
    - "laboratoria przyszłości"

kontrast:
  # wszystkie pozostałe przedmioty tego samego etapu, poza wymienionymi niżej
  przedmioty_wyklucz:            # treść w języku obcym – nie nadaje się na kontrast polszczyzny
    - "Język obcy: angielski"
    - "Język obcy: niemiecki"
    - "Język obcy: francuski"
    - "Język obcy: hiszpański"
    - "Język obcy: włoski"
    - "Język obcy: rosyjski"
    - "Język obcy nowożytny"
    - "Język mniejszości narodowej lub etnicznej"
    - "Język mniejszości narodowej – język niemiecki"
    - "Język regionalny – język kaszubski"
  przedmioty_poza_celem: ["Matematyka"]   # zostają w kontraście, nie będą celem analizy

czyszczenie:
  segmenty_do_statystyk: [tytul, tresc, definicja, cwiczenie, podpis]   # 'alt' (opisy WCAG) poza statystykami
  szablon_min_materialow: 25     # zdanie powtórzone w >= tylu materiałach etapu = szablon platformy
  szablon_max_slow: 14

klasa_szacowana:
  # Katalog ZPE zna tylko etap ("4-8"). Klasa jest SZACOWANA z działu tematycznego.
  # Podstawa programowa biologii nie dzieli treści na klasy; poniższy podział to konwencja
  # typowych programów nauczania (kl. 5: komórka, bakterie, protisty, grzyby, rośliny;
  # kl. 6: zwierzęta; kl. 7: człowiek; kl. 8: genetyka, ewolucja, ekologia).
  bloki:
    5: ["komórk", "fotosyntez", "bakteri", "protist", "grzyb", "porost", "mch[yuaóe]", "mszak", "paproc", "paprotnik",
        "skrzyp", "widłak", "nagonasienn", "okrytonasienn", "tkank\\w+ roślinn", "korze[nń]", "łodyg", "liś[cć]", "liści",
        "kwiat", "nasion", "owoc", "wirus", "mikroskop", "roślin", "kiełkowani", "zapyleni", "glon"]
    6: ["zwierz", "płazi[ńn]c", "nicien", "pierścienic", "stawonog", "owad", "skorupiak", "pajęczak", "mięczak",
        "ślimak", "małż", "głowonog", "ryb[ayom]?\\b", "płaz[yaóie]", "gad[yaóie]\\w*\\b", "ptak", "ptas", "ssak",
        "parzydełkow", "tkank\\w+ zwierzęc", "kręgowc", "bezkręgowc", "zmiennociepln", "stałociepln", "tasiem", "dżdżownic"]
    7: ["układ\\w* (krwionośn|oddechow|pokarmow|nerwow|hormonaln|dokrewn|wydalnicz|moczow|rozrodcz|odpornościow|kostn|mięśniow|ruchu|krążeni|limfatyczn)",
        "człowiek", "ludzk", "skór", "szkielet", "mięśni", "krew\\b", "krwi\\b", "serc", "odżywiani", "witamin", "hormon",
        "neuron", "mózg", "zmysł", "\\boko\\b", "\\bucho\\b", "chorob", "zdrowi", "ciąż", "dojrzewani", "homeostaz",
        "odpornoś", "szczepi", "uzależni", "trawieni", "płuc", "nerk", "kręgosłup", "zęb", "pierwsz\\w+ pomoc"]
    8: ["\\bgen[yuaóe]?\\w{0,3}\\b", "genetyk", "genotyp", "fenotyp", "\\bDNA\\b", "chromosom", "dziedzicz", "allel", "mutacj",
        "ewolucj", "dob[oó]r\\w* naturaln", "ekosystem", "populacj", "łańcuch\\w* pokarmow", "sie[cć]\\w* pokarmow",
        "biocenoz", "ochron\\w+ przyrod", "ochron\\w+ środowisk", "różnorodnoś\\w+ biologiczn", "konkurencj", "pasożytnictw",
        "drapieżnictw", "symbioz", "zasob\\w+ przyrod", "park\\w* narodow", "gatunk\\w+ chronion", "rezerwat", "ekologi",
        "tolerancj\\w+ ekologiczn", "nisz\\w+ ekologiczn", "antropogen", "krzyżówk\\w+ genetyczn", "grup\\w+ krwi"]

narzedzia:
  tager_produkcyjny: spacy_morfeusz   # wybierany po ocenie 4.1; używany dla całego korpusu
  spacy_model: pl_core_news_lg
  stanza_dir: resources/tools/stanza_resources
  procesy: 8

kandydaci:
  max_dlugosc: 4
  min_frekw_cel: 3               # minimalna frekwencja w korpusie docelowym
  min_materialow: 2              # ... i liczba materiałów
  top_do_llm: 1500               # ilu najlepszych kandydatów każdej metody idzie do klasyfikacji LLM
  ogolne_do_llm: 1500            # kandydaci do puli ogólnej (szerokie rozproszenie po przedmiotach)

llm:
  wersja_promptu: v1
  modele_porownywane: [claude-haiku-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5]
  model_rozstrzygajacy: claude-opus-5-5
  model_ekstrakcji: claude-sonnet-5-5
  limit_kosztu_usd: 100
  batch: true
  cache_ttl: 1h
  parametry:                     # ustawienia myślenia wg dokumentacji „Effort” (2026-11-13)
    claude-haiku-5-5: {thinking: {type: disabled}}
    claude-sonnet-5-5: {thinking: {type: between_tools}}
    claude-opus-5-5: {effort: medium, min_max_tokens: 4000}   # myślenia adaptacyjnego nie da się wyłączyć

zloty_zbior:
  n: 400

pseudoslowa:
  n_szablonow: 240
  kandydatow_na_szablon: 6
  czeste_slowo_zipf: 3.0         # próg "częstego słowa" dla filtra literówek

title: Pseudowords
text:
Templates are single real words from the general pool, stratified by length and syllable count. Each of the four generators proposes pseudowords for a template; filters then reject anything that is, or looks too much like, a real Polish word. imbir is a published ready-made list, sampled at random, so its rows are not derived from the template they sit next to.

WarningThe unipseudo rows of this run are not usable



The 240 kept unipseudo rows are copies of 3 strings (taliży, sensja, chcisy), repeated for every template. Step 7 starts the UniPseudo generator but does not read what it prints. It then takes the first rows of whichever CSV file lies in resources/pseudo/unipseudo/, and in this run that was the six-letter smoke-test file. The strings are therefore neither matched to their templates nor newly generated. Count 852 distinct pseudowords from the other three generators as the usable result of this run. The step needs fixing before the full run.

title: Candidates
text:
3 513 candidates passed the frequency filters. 925 of them were labelled by the language models; the rest carry only the rule-based pre-label (label_source = rule), and do_llm in kategoria means the rules could not decide either. None of the labels has been checked by a human.






WarningTwo form columns



forma_kandydata is the string the statistics were computed for. forma_podstawowa is the same string unless the language model returned a different base form: this happened for 122 candidates, and for 60 of them the model’s form has a different number of words (for example a single adjective replaced by a whole two-word term), so the counts in the row do not describe the string in forma_podstawowa. Because of these replacements 144 rows share their forma_podstawowa with another row. Filter form_changed = yes to see them.


Type in the boxes under the column names to filter a single column (for example T3 under kategoria), click a header to sort, and use Columns to show the hidden rank and per-model columns.


Source file: kandydaci.csv (view · download).








NoteColumn glossary












Column
Meaning




forma_podstawowa
Base (dictionary) form of the candidate. Where the LLM returned a different base form, this is the LLM’s form; compare with forma_kandydata.


forma_kandydata
The candidate exactly as extracted in step 4. All counts, scores and ranks in the row were computed for this string.


form_changed
Derived for this page: yes if forma_podstawowa differs from forma_kandydata.


kategoria
Label used for the pools: the LLM label where available, otherwise the rule-based pre-label.


label_source
Derived for this page: LLM if kategoria comes from the models, rule if only from the rule-based pre-label.


pojecie
Short concept label from the LLM, shared by variants and synonyms.


obrazowalnosc
LLM judgement whether the concept can be shown in a picture or diagram (tak, czesciowo, nie).


dlugosc
Number of words in forma_kandydata.


cls
Inflectional class of the lemma from Morfeusz2 (subst noun, adj adjective, ger gerund, ppas/pact participles, fin/inf/praet verb forms, adv adverb); mwu for multiword candidates.


freq_cel
Occurrences in the target corpus (biology).


freq_kontrast
Occurrences in the contrast corpus (other subjects of the same school stage).


n_mat_cel
Number of target materials containing the candidate.


n_przedmiotow
Number of contrast subjects in which the candidate occurs (dispersion).


freq_kwjp
Lemma frequency in KWJP100 (general Polish, CC BY 4.0), summed over inflectional classes.


zipf_wordfreq
Zipf frequency from wordfreq (0 = not found; single words only).


n_mat_kontrast
Number of contrast materials containing the candidate.


n_klas_cel
Number of distinct estimated grades among target materials containing the candidate.


ll_vs_kontrast
Log-likelihood keyness, target vs contrast corpus; negative when relatively rarer in biology.


log_ratio_kontrast
Log₂ ratio of relative frequencies, target vs contrast (smoothing 0.5).


ll_vs_kwjp
Log-likelihood keyness against KWJP100 (reference size is a convention; use for ranking only).


log_ratio_kwjp
Log₂ ratio of relative frequencies, target vs KWJP100.


simple_maths_kwjp
Kilgarriff’s Simple Maths keyness against KWJP100 (per-million rates, N = 1).


tfidf_biol
Relative frequency in biology × log(1 + subjects / (1 + n_przedmiotow)).


rozproszenie
Same value as n_przedmiotow (higher = more cross-subject, i.e. more T2-like).


pmi
Pointwise mutual information of the first two lemmas of a multiword candidate (0 for single words).


logdice
logDice of the first two lemmas of a multiword candidate (0 for single words).


rank_ll_vs_kontrast
Rank of the candidate by ll_vs_kontrast (1 = best).


rank_log_ratio_kontrast
Rank of the candidate by log_ratio_kontrast (1 = best).


rank_simple_maths_kwjp
Rank of the candidate by simple_maths_kwjp (1 = best).


rank_ll_vs_kwjp
Rank of the candidate by ll_vs_kwjp (1 = best).


rank_tfidf_biol
Rank of the candidate by tfidf_biol (1 = best).


rank_pmi
Rank of the candidate by pmi (1 = best).


rank_logdice
Rank of the candidate by logdice (1 = best).


cvalue
TermoPL C-value on the target corpus (0 = not returned by TermoPL).


rank_cvalue
Rank of the candidate by cvalue (1 = best).


termopl_ok
Whether TermoPL ran successfully in this run.


etykieta_regulowa
Rule-based pre-label from frequency thresholds (T3?, T2?, T1?, do_llm = undecided).


kategoria_final
LLM label (empty if the candidate was not sent to the LLM).


forma_podstawowa_llm
Base form returned by the LLM.


do_przegladu
True if the models disagreed or one had low confidence, so Opus adjudicated.


haiku_5_5_kategoria
Label from Claude Haiku 5.5.


haiku_5_5_pewnosc
Self-reported confidence of Claude Haiku 5.5 (wysoka, srednia, niska).


sonnet_5_5_kategoria
Label from Claude Sonnet 5.5.


sonnet_5_5_pewnosc
Self-reported confidence of Claude Sonnet 5.5 (wysoka, srednia, niska).


opus_5_5_kategoria
Label from Claude Opus 5.5.


opus_5_5_pewnosc
Self-reported confidence of Claude Opus 5.5 (wysoka, srednia, niska).

Licence points that need your decision

SUBTLEX-PL is non-commercial and share-alike (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, subtlex-pl_license.txt). The 2015 paper says the database is “freely available for research purposes”. Anything derived from it has to carry the same licence.
NKJP1M licence version is inconsistent. The README inside the archive says CC BY 3.0 PL (its English paragraph adds “Attribution 3.0 Unported” and links to the unported 3.0 deed), nkjp.pl says CC-BY 4.0, and the CLIP download page says just “CC-BY”. All three are attribution-only, but I did not pick one. The four NKJP1M entries have status licence_unclear in manifest.json; the files are present.
NKJP 1-grams are “made available on CC-BY licence” with no version number on the page.
wordfreq data is share-alike (CC BY-SA 4.0).
KWJP: the CC BY 4.0 statement is in the repository README.md only; the repository has no LICENSE file (GitHub API reports license: null).

1. NKJP (Narodowy Korpus Języka Polskiego)
What is downloadable today:

A ready-made form frequency list: the 1-gram file from https://zil.ipipan.waw.pl/NKJPNGrams.
No ready-made lemma frequency list was found. The pages checked were https://zil.ipipan.waw.pl/NKJPNGrams, https://clip.ipipan.waw.pl/NationalCorpusOfPolish, https://zil.ipipan.waw.pl/DistrNKJP and https://nkjp.pl/index.php?page=N&lang=0 for N = 0…25. A lemma list can be derived from the manually annotated 1-million subcorpus, which is downloadable, so that was done (section 1b).
https://nkjp.nlp.ipipan.waw.pl/ (“NKJP 300M”, re-tagged in 2020) is a query interface; its landing page offers no download link.
https://zil.ipipan.waw.pl/DistrNKJP offers two redistributable subcorpora as raw corpora (5SCAL-free.tar, nkjp-wikipedia.tar.gz). They are not frequency lists and were not downloaded.

Caveats, checked in the file:

Tokens are whitespace-delimited, so punctuation stays attached. proces (22,118), proces, (1,421) and proces. (926) are separate entries; . (93,298) and , (68,284) also occur as entries of their own. Mandera et al. (2015) describe handling this by “summing frequencies of all forms that were identical after removing punctuation marks attached to some of the forms”. The second row of the verification table shows what that does for four words.
No entry contains upper-case characters; 1,413,827 of the 5,364,398 entries are purely alphabetic (194,119,824 tokens).
Parse with line.lstrip().split(' ', 1). Splitting on single spaces breaks because of the padding.

Format: TSV, UTF-8, LF, header row, sorted by descending frequency. Each file sums to 1,215,513.
How the counts are made:

The unit counted is one NKJP segment (<seg>). Punctuation is its own segment, and so are agglutinates such as em in zrobiłem.
The lemma and class are the manually disambiguated ones: the choice pointer in <f name="disamb"> is resolved to its <fs type="lex"> (base, ctag). All 1,215,513 segments resolved this way.
Lemma case is kept as annotated, so proper names are capitalised. orth_lc is the segment lower-cased.
Nothing is filtered: punctuation, numbers and foreign strings are included. The only normalisation is trimming and collapsing whitespace inside a segment’s form and lemma, needed because one URL segment contains a TAB.
In the NKJP tagset verb forms belong to separate classes (fin, praet, inf, ger, ppas, …), so one verb is spread over several rows of the lemma × ctag file; the lemma-only file sums them, and also merges homonyms of different classes.

2. SUBTLEX-PL (Mandera, Keuleers, Wodniecka & Brysbaert, 2015)
Where it is today:

http://crr.ugent.be/subtlex-pl (the URL given in the paper) redirects to https and returns HTTP 404. https://crr.ugent.be/ shows a notice that the website was removed and is “under reconstruction”, with a pointer to the Internet Archive.
The files are on OSF: https://osf.io/5a76z/ (project “SUBTLEX-PL”, contributor Marc Brysbaert, created 2023-12-18). The project wiki says: “These files are the same as the ones referred to in the article.”
All files below were downloaded from OSF on 2026-11-13, and each local sha256 equals the hash reported by the OSF API.

Licence: the OSF licence field is “Other” with the text “Please see the file named license.txt in the OSF Storage of this project.” That file (https://osf.io/qra8w/, saved as subtlex-pl_license.txt) says:

The materials on this website is subject to the following CC license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International

The paper’s abstract says “The database is freely available for research purposes”.
Corpus (stated in the paper, a copy of which is in the OSF project): 27,767 subtitle files after de-duplication, “about 146 million tokens (individual strings, including punctuation marks, numbers, etc.), out of which 101 million tokens (449,300 types) were accepted as correctly spelled Polish words” by Aspell. “All words were converted to lowercase before spell-checking.” Lemmas and POS come from automatic tagging with TaKIPI and Morfeusz.

Format: TAB-separated despite the .csv name; UTF-8, no BOM, LF, header row, no quoting; 25 columns.
Unit: orthographic form, lower-cased (no row contains upper case). capit.freq records how often the form was capitalised in the subtitles.
subtlex-pl.csv is the full list: 987,911 rows, freq sums to 145,982,416 (computed). It includes numbers and non-words; rows with spellcheck=1 and alphabetical=1 number 449,302 types and 101,060,958 tokens (computed), matching the paper.
subtlex-pl-cd-3.csv is the subset of strings found in at least 3 films: 377,843 rows, freq sums to 144,937,876. The OSF wiki recommends this subset to new users (as the .xlsx).

Format: TAB-separated, UTF-8, no BOM, LF, header row; 6 columns: lemma, pos, spelling, freq, cd.count, cd.

3. KWJP (Korpus Współczesnego Języka Polskiego, dekada 2011–2020)
A downloadable frequency list exists.

https://kwjp.pl/lists/ is an online browser of the frequency lists. Its help page https://kwjp.pl/lists/doc/about/ ends with “Listy frekwencyjne KWJP można również pobrać z repozytorium”, linking to https://github.com/ipipan/kwjp100-varia/tree/main/freqlists.
That repository holds 48 gzipped CSV lists: words and 2/3/4-grams × {lemma, orth, orth_lc} × {all, fakt, fikcja, publicystyka}. The three single-word lists for the whole balanced corpus were downloaded. The genre-specific word lists (2.4–6.5 MB each) and the n-gram lists were not.
CLARIN-PL repository: a search for “KWJP” through https://clarin-pl.eu/dspace/server/api/discover/search/objects?query=KWJP returned 0 results (the old https://clarin-pl.eu/dspace/discover?query=KWJP URL returns 404).

Licence: the repository README.md says “Ze wszystkich zasobów zamieszczonych w tym repozytorium można korzystać na zasadach licencji CC-BY 4.0 (Creative Commons Attribution 4.0)” — https://github.com/ipipan/kwjp100-varia/blob/main/README.md. There is no separate LICENSE file.
Corpus (stated at https://kwjp.pl/overview): texts from 2011–2020; “over one billion words, 100 million of which have been included in the balanced corpus”, made up of 35% news and journalistic texts, 30% fiction and 35% non-fiction. It has no spoken or internet texts. The requested citation is Kieraś et al., Język Polski 105(2):5–20, 2025, doi 10.31286/JP.001055.
How the lists were built (stated on the help page): compiled automatically from the balanced corpus using automatic lemmatisation and tagging, so they may contain errors; only words in Latin letters (optionally with a hyphen); only units occurring at least 5 times in the whole corpus.
Files were fetched from commit-pinned URLs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ipipan/kwjp100-varia/26d82bd8b906dfed1cfcf8f903b1650b56daeabf/freqlists/<file> on 2026-11-13 (the lists were committed on 2024-04-15). Git blob hashes match the GitHub API listing.

4. wordfreq 3.1.1 (Python library, already in the venv)
Nothing was downloaded. Facts below come from the installed package (wordfreq-3.1.1.dist-info/METADATA, which embeds the README) and were cross-checked against https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq/blob/master/README.md.

It runs: wordfreq.word_frequency('fotosynteza', 'pl') returns 1.74e-07 (Zipf 2.24).
Sources for Polish (README table row Polish pl 6 Yes │ Yes Yes Yes - Yes Yes Yes -): six domains from the “Exquisite Corpus” project.

Wikipedia
Subtitles: “OPUS OpenSubtitles 2018 and SUBTLEX”. The SUBTLEX lists the README names are US, UK, CH, DE and NL; SUBTLEX-PL is not among them.
News: NewsCrawl 2014 and GlobalVoices
Web: OSCAR
Twitter
Reddit
Not used for Polish: Google Books.

How they are combined: per word, the sources giving the highest and lowest frequency are dropped, the rest averaged, and the list rescaled to sum to 1. There is therefore no single corpus size.
Unit: orthographic forms, not lemmas. Text is tokenised with a regex tokenizer following Unicode UAX #29 and case-folded: Proces and proces return the same value, and tokenize('Fotosynteza i KOMÓRKA', 'pl') gives ['fotosynteza', 'i', 'komórka']. Inflected forms have their own entries (komórka 5.25e-06, komórki 2.95e-05).
Resolution: frequencies are stored in bins of 0.01 on the Zipf scale. Polish has a “large” list (used by default as best; 453,320 entries, down to Zipf 1.0) and a “small” one. Multi-digit numbers are pooled by shape.
Licence: code Apache-2.0 (LICENSE.txt); the README says it “includes data files that may be redistributed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 license”. See https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq#license.
Data file: .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/wordfreq/data/large_pl.msgpack.gz, 2,368,608 bytes, sha256 fac63e49c49ea2e39dd8a48152d7e54cec0920abbc59993088063ed5d9b528c2.

title: JUTRO pilot: subject vocabulary and pseudowords
text:
ImportantStatus



Everything here is a candidate list produced by an automatic process on a sample of 50 biology materials (run probka50). No list has been validated by subject or language specialists, and no model label has been checked against human annotation yet.

title: JUTRO pilot: subject vocabulary and pseudowords
text:
Problem
Pupils with a migration background may fail a subject test for two different reasons: weak general Polish, or missing subject concepts despite adequate language. JUTRO aims to separate those barriers with three modules: recognition of general words against pseudowords, word associations, and matching subject terms to images.
This pilot builds the word material for biology (grades 5–8) from the teaching materials of the Integrated Educational Platform (ZPE): a pool of subject terms, a pool of general and school vocabulary, concept groups, and pseudowords for a LexTALE-style test.

One command runs eight steps. Each step reads the files written by the earlier ones, so a step can be re-run on its own, and every number on this site is read from a metrics file that a step saved.

title: JUTRO pilot: subject vocabulary and pseudowords
text:
Limits



This is a sample run. Counts and rankings will change on the full corpus.
The grade of a material is estimated from topic keywords; the ZPE catalogue only records the stage (grades 4–8).
Only 925 of 3513 candidates were labelled by the LLMs. The pools also contain candidates that carry only the rule-based pre-label; the label_source column on the data pages tells them apart.
For 122 candidates the language model returned a base form different from the extracted one, and for 60 of them with a different number of words. The statistics in those rows belong to the extracted string (forma_kandydata), and the same forma_podstawowa can appear in several rows of a pool. See the Candidates page.
The silver standard (ZPE glossaries) is incomplete, so precision@K against it is only useful for comparing methods.
SUBTLEX-PL is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and is used for comparison metrics only; it does not enter the published lists.
The UA/RU similarity flag on pseudowords compares against a built-in list of ten transliterated words. It is a placeholder for review by bilingual staff.
The unipseudo pseudowords of this run are not usable: the 240 rows are copies of 3 strings. See the note on the Pseudowords page.

title: Pseudoword resources
text:
Full notes


Checked and downloaded on 2026-11-13 (machine: macOS arm64, Python 3.12.2 venv at ../../.venv, R 4.4.1). Everything below was verified by fetching or running it on that date; anything that could not be verified is marked NOT VERIFIED. Machine-readable version: manifest.json (hashes, sizes, licences, status per file).
Total size of this directory: about 54 MB. No system packages and no R packages were installed (Rlib/ was not needed and was not created). Nothing was written into the venv.

1. Wuggy (Python package) and the official Polish plugin

What exists

Installed package: wuggy 1.1.2 (PyPI project Wuggy, wheel uploaded 2024-02-20, the newest release on PyPI; https://pypi.org/project/Wuggy/). Source: https://github.com/WuggyCode/wuggy. Licence MIT (wuggy-1.1.2.dist-info/LICENSE, “Copyright (c) 2020 Emmanuel Keuleers”; GitHub API reports MIT; https://github.com/WuggyCode/wuggy/blob/master/LICENSE). GitHub master (commit 25de4ac1a608913bcdd633f312f3ac7dd2fead4a, 2026-04-17) is at version 1.2.0 in setup.py and is not on PyPI; it adds orthographic_lithuanian and a GUI-related plugin path.
An official Polish plugin exists: orthographic_polish. The official names hard-coded in 1.1.2 (WuggyGenerator().supported_official_language_plugin_names) are: orthographic_basque, orthographic_dutch, orthographic_english, orthographic_french, orthographic_german, orthographic_italian, orthographic_polish, orthographic_serbian_cyrillic, orthographic_serbian_latin, orthographic_spanish, orthographic_vietnamese, orthographic_estonian, phonetic_english_celex, phonetic_english_cmu, phonetic_french, phonetic_italian.
Plugin data repository: https://github.com/WuggyCode/wuggy_language_plugin_data (branch master, commit 2968223983626c4a178cda7ea071c082dcaba3fb, 2026-04-16). The orthographic_polish/ folder was last changed in the initial commit 43258ad8a900dc26dcdb18d16d371479b7fa1d0d (2020-12-14).



How plugins are downloaded and stored (read from wuggy/generators/wuggygenerator.py, 1.1.2)

WuggyGenerator.load(name) looks for <site-packages>/wuggy/plugins/language_data/<name>/; if the folder is missing it calls download_language_plugin(name), which asks for y/n on stdin unless called with auto_download=True.
The download fetches exactly two files with urllib.request.urlopen from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WuggyCode/wuggy_language_plugin_data/master/<name>/<name>.py and .../<name>/<name>.txt and writes them into that language_data/<name>/ folder inside site-packages.
WuggyGenerator.remove_downloaded_language_plugins() deletes the whole language_data folder.
Problem on this machine: the venv’s Python has no CA bundle configured, so the built-in download fails with ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate. It works when SSL_CERT_FILE points at certifi’s bundle (tested, see below). A failed download leaves an empty language_data/orthographic_polish/ folder behind, and because load() only checks that the folder exists, it must be deleted before retrying.



Plugin file format and API
A plugin is a folder with two files:

<name>.py defining a subclass of wuggy.plugins.baselanguageplugin.BaseLanguagePlugin (official plugins must name the class OfficialLanguagePlugin). Required members: default_data, default_neighbor_lexicon, default_word_lexicon, default_lookup_lexicon (file names, resolved relative to the folder of the .py file) and transform(self, input_sequence, frequency=1). The Polish plugin implements transform as self.pre_transform(input_sequence, frequency=frequency, language=self) and supplies oncpattern, a regex with three groups (onset, nucleus, coda) applied to each syllable. Inherited from the base class: output modes plain, syllabic, segmental, pass; statistics lexicality, ned1, old20, overlap, overlap_ratio, plain_length, transition_frequencies.
<name>.txt, UTF-8, one entry per line, three tab-separated columns: word <TAB> word-syl-la-bi-fied (hyphens between syllables) <TAB> frequency. The same file serves as bigram-chain training data, lookup lexicon (word to syllabification), word lexicon (lexicality check) and neighbour lexicon (OLD20, ned1). For the lexicons Wuggy reads the last column as a float and keeps entries with frequency >= 0. For the bigram chain, BigramChain.load in 1.1.2 sets frequency = 1 for every line, so each entry counts once (type counts); the frequency column does not weight the transition frequencies. The Wuggy documentation calls the third column “occurrence per million words”; in the Polish file the values are proportions that sum to 1.000000.

To use a custom or modified plugin: g.load("any_name", local_language_plugin=MyPlugin()). The data folder is the folder containing the class’s .py file. The official docs (documentation/baselanguageplugin/baselanguageplugin.md in the Wuggy repo) say to copy the official .py/.txt and replace from ...baselanguageplugin import BaseLanguagePlugin with from wuggy import BaseLanguagePlugin. wuggy_plugins/load_local_plugin.py here achieves the same without editing the official file.


The Polish plugin (wuggy_plugins/orthographic_polish/)

orthographic_polish.py (1,017 bytes): header comment “Subsyllabic Polish, by Paweł Mandera, pawel.mandera@ugent.be”. Nucleus pattern: ia|ie|io|iu|ą|ę|a|e|i|o|u|y.
orthographic_polish.txt (39,841,583 bytes): 834,141 entries, all lower-case, no duplicate words, every line has 3 columns. Frequencies range from 9.828e-09 to 0.0283 (nie) and sum to 1.000000.
Source corpus: NOT documented in the plugin, the plugin repository (no README) or the Wuggy docs, so it is NOT VERIFIED. Observations only: the author is the first author of SUBTLEX-PL (Mandera et al. 2015, doi:10.3758/s13428-014-0489-4); the lexicon has more types than the 449,300 reported for SUBTLEX-PL, and its frequency values are not integer multiples of the smallest value, so it is not a plain count list from one corpus. Ask the maintainers before citing a source.
Licence of the plugin data: none stated. The repository has no licence file (GitHub API license: null, /license endpoint returns 404) and the files carry no licence header. The MIT licence of the wuggy package is in a different repository and does not mention the language data. Flagged as unclear.
Quirk: ó is missing from the nucleus pattern. For 36,607 of 834,141 entries (4.4%) at least one syllable does not match the onset-nucleus-coda regex, and Wuggy then treats the whole syllable as an “onset” segment (e.g. po-ró-wnać becomes segments p|o||ró|||wn|a|ć). Templates containing ó therefore get a much narrower and odder candidate set (see porównać below).
The lexicon is large and contains rare forms; lexicality == "N" only means “not in this file”. Candidates should still be screened against a dictionary before use as LexTALE nonwords.



Exact calls that worked
Loading the plugin from this directory (nothing written to the venv), from wuggy_plugins/:
from load_local_plugin import load_generator      # helper in this folder
import random
g = load_generator("orthographic_polish")         # about 10.5 s
random.seed(20261113)                             # see "Reproducibility"
matches = g.generate_classic(["komora"], ncandidates_per_sequence=5, max_search_time_per_sequence=30)
# each match: {"word", "segments", "pseudoword", "statistics": {...}, "difference_statistics": {...}}
load_generator is equivalent to:
import importlib.util, sys
from wuggy import WuggyGenerator
name = "orthographic_polish"
mod_name = f"wuggy.plugins.language_data.{name}.{name}"
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(mod_name, f"wuggy_plugins/{name}/{name}.py")
mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); sys.modules[mod_name] = mod; spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
g = WuggyGenerator(); g.load(name, local_language_plugin=mod.OfficialLanguagePlugin())
Smoke test command (about 20 s in total):
. /Users/michalpalinski/kompetencje_jezykowe/.venv/bin/activate
cd /Users/michalpalinski/kompetencje_jezykowe/resources/pseudo/wuggy_plugins
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python smoke_test_polish.py
Output (smoke_test_polish_output.log, .json); all three template words are in the lexicon:







template (syllabification in lexicon)
5 pseudowords (OLD20)




komora (ko-mo-ra)
kanory (1.80), kasory (1.75), karory (1.80), kabory (1.80), kawory (1.70)


wynik (wy-nik)
wynył (1.80), wynyć (1.80), wyneł (1.95), wyneć (1.95), wynać (1.75)


porównać (po-ró-wnać)
połódnał (2.90), połóścał (3.00), połówcał (2.80), pomódnał (2.90), pomówcał (2.75)



The official download path was also tested, on a copy of the package in /tmp so that the venv stayed untouched; it produced byte-identical plugin files (same sha256):
SSL_CERT_FILE=$(python -c "import certifi; print(certifi.where())") python -c '
from wuggy import WuggyGenerator
g = WuggyGenerator()
g.download_language_plugin("orthographic_polish", auto_download=True)
g.load("orthographic_polish")
print([m["pseudoword"] for m in g.generate_classic(["komora"], ncandidates_per_sequence=5)])'
Without SSL_CERT_FILE this fails on this machine with the certificate error quoted above. Run against the real venv it would write the 40 MB plugin into .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/wuggy/plugins/language_data/.


Reproducibility
Wuggy shuffles its start keys with Python’s global random module (wuggy/utilities/bigramchain.py). Without a seed, repeated runs gave different pseudowords for the same template; PYTHONHASHSEED=0 did not fix it. Calling random.seed(<int>) right before generate_classic gave identical output within a process and across two separate processes. generate_classic also stops at max_search_time_per_sequence (default 10 s), so a slower machine can return fewer candidates.




2. Dołżycka, Nikadon & Formanowicz (2022)
Paper: Dołżycka, J. D., Nikadon, J., & Formanowicz, M. (2022). Constructing Pseudowords with Constraints on Morphological Features - Application for Polish Pseudonouns and Pseudoverbs. Journal of Psycholinguistic Research, 51(6), 1247-1265. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10936-022-09884-6. Pipeline language: IPython / Emacs Org (#+BEGIN_SRC ipython), not a standalone CLI. Stages prepare template word lists, export TSV for Wuggy, then read Wuggy’s output TSV back and filter/merge.

Algorithm (as implemented in generatePseudo.R)
All source words have the same length L. For trigrams: pick a random source word and keep its first 3 letters; then, for each following position, take the last 2 letters built so far, find all source words with those 2 letters at that same position, and draw the next letter in proportion to how often it follows there. Bigram variant: same with 1 letter of context. A candidate is kept if it is not a source word, not in the exclusion list, not a duplicate, and passes the constraints. For a named language the app uses, from the WorldLex table, source words with BlogFreqPm > 0.5 and the exclusion list of all entries of that length. Default algorithm: bigram up to length 5, trigram from 6. Constraint presets in the R app for Polish: at most 3 consecutive consonants and at most 2 identical consecutive letters (the live Django site reported no presets for Polish).

pseudo-word

title: Pools and concepts
text:
The pools are the candidates split by label: T3 (subject terms) and T1/T2 (everyday and school vocabulary). For each subject term the pipeline picks one general-pool item of the same length in words and the closest Zipf frequency. label_source shows whether the label comes from the language models or only from the rule-based pre-label. Nothing here has been checked by a human.






WarningTwo form columns



forma_kandydata is the string the statistics were computed for; forma_podstawowa is the language model’s base form where it returned a different one (form_changed = yes: 53 rows in the subject pool, 37 in the general pool). As a result the same forma_podstawowa can appear in more than one row (62 such rows in the subject pool, 51 in the general pool), and matching between the pools is done on forma_podstawowa.


Filter with the boxes under the table, sort by clicking a header, and use Columns to show the hidden columns.

Subject pool (T3)General pool (T1/T2)Concepts


1455 terms; 415 labelled by the language models, 1040 by rules only.


Source file: pula_przedmiotowa.csv (view · download).

Column
Meaning




forma_podstawowa
Base (dictionary) form of the candidate. Where the LLM returned a different base form, this is the LLM’s form; compare with forma_kandydata.

The candidate exactly as extracted in step 4. All counts, scores and ranks in the row were computed for this string.


form_changed
Derived for this page: yes if forma_podstawowa differs from forma_kandydata.

LLM judgement whether the concept can be shown in a picture or diagram (tak, czesciowo, nie).

Number of words in forma_kandydata.

n_przedmiotow
Number of contrast subjects in which the candidate occurs (dispersion).

Lemma frequency in KWJP100 (general Polish, CC BY 4.0), summed over inflectional classes.

Zipf frequency from wordfreq (0 = not found; single words only).


n_mat_kontrast
Number of contrast materials containing the candidate.


n_klas_cel
Number of distinct estimated grades among target materials containing the candidate.


ll_vs_kontrast
Log-likelihood keyness, target vs contrast corpus; negative when relatively rarer in biology.


log_ratio_kontrast
Log₂ ratio of relative frequencies, target vs contrast (smoothing 0.5).


ll_vs_kwjp

log_ratio_kwjp
Log₂ ratio of relative frequencies, target vs KWJP100.


simple_maths_kwjp
Kilgarriff’s Simple Maths keyness against KWJP100 (per-million rates, N = 1).


tfidf_biol
Relative frequency in biology × log(1 + subjects / (1 + n_przedmiotow)).


rozproszenie
Same value as n_przedmiotow (higher = more cross-subject, i.e. more T2-like).


pmi
Pointwise mutual information of the first two lemmas of a multiword candidate (0 for single words).


logdice
logDice of the first two lemmas of a multiword candidate (0 for single words).


rank_ll_vs_kontrast
Rank of the candidate by ll_vs_kontrast (1 = best).


rank_log_ratio_kontrast

rank_pmi
Rank of the candidate by pmi (1 = best).


rank_logdice
Rank of the candidate by logdice (1 = best).


cvalue
TermoPL C-value on the target corpus (0 = not returned by TermoPL).


rank_cvalue
Rank of the candidate by cvalue (1 = best).


termopl_ok
Whether TermoPL ran successfully in this run.


etykieta_regulowa
Rule-based pre-label from frequency thresholds (T3?, T2?, T1?, do_llm = undecided).


forma_join
Candidate form as sent to the LLM (join key).


kategoria_final
LLM label (empty if the candidate was not sent to the LLM).


forma_podstawowa_llm
Base form returned by the LLM.


do_przegladu
True if the models disagreed or one had low confidence, so Opus adjudicated.


haiku_5_5_kategoria
